title: OpenAI ChatCompletions schema hydrator and response shape enforcer
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: Customers integrating Redwood API with OpenAI Chat Completions expect parity for request/response shapes when using third-party SDKs and older chat tooling. Existing edge cases cause differences in tool/function-calling payloads, streaming delta framing, and structured output JSON fields which break downstream webhooks and eval suites. This ticket implements a 'schema hydrator' layer that takes incoming OpenAI-style ChatCompletions requests, enriches/normalizes them into Redwood's internal canonical request shape, and then enforces an output shaper on responses so that we can present predictable OpenAI-compatible responses for hosted and dedicated tenants.

Scope: Implement request-side hydrator (role/message normalization, metadata mapping, tool call hint extraction, streaming flag reconciliation) and response-side shape enforcer (delta framing, content vs function call fields, finish_reason normalization, tool_call serialization). Work targets hosted API and Dedicated endpoints behind the compatibility route. Not in scope: full migration of older customers to redirect to native chat API, or UI console changes.

Goals: reduce customer-reported incompatibility regressions by 90% for ChatCompletions compatibility tests, maintain streaming SSE framing parity for SDKs that expect 'choices[].delta', and provide stable deterministic function-calling responses for automated tool runners.

Design decisions: adopt a two-step approach: 1) lightweight request rewrite that keeps original payload in request_context for audit and replay; 2) response shaping as a deterministic post-processing stage that can be toggled per-customer or per-route. We favor small, clearly versioned transformation functions rather than a single monolithic adapter to ease testing and future rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Incoming OpenAI ChatCompletions v1 requests are accepted and recorded with original payload in request_context metadata.
2) Tool/function calling hints from messages (structured 'tool:' markers, JSON schema hints) are extracted into standardized tool_call hints in internal request model.
3) Streaming responses expose identical SSE framing to our OpenAI compatibility test harness (choices[].delta streaming events and final choices[].finish_reason).
4) Function call outputs are serialized to match OpenAI shape (name, arguments as stringified JSON) and are included in final 'choices' entry with consistent indexing.
5) Compatibility toggle per-customer route works and is covered by integration tests.
6) No regression on native Redwood chat API behavior (sanity smoke tests pass).
implementation_notes:
- Add request hydrator middleware in compat routing layer that runs prior to rate-limiting and batching.
- Persist original openai_payload to request_context as base64-encoded string for audit/logging.
- Extend streaming encoder to emit 'delta' frames for role/content/tool_call fragments; ensure chunk boundaries preserve UTF-8 and valid JSON when needed.
- Introduce ResponseShapeEnforcer class with a small DSL for field mappings and finish_reason normalization.
- Add unit tests for edge cases: missing roles, assistant messages with function_call present, arrays of choices with partial tokens, tokenization boundary tests.
- Performance targets: middleware should add <0.5ms p50 overhead in synthetic benchmark; streaming path must preserve p95 token latency within current SLO.
- Rollout plan: feature-flag behind 'openai_compat_v2' and gradual ramp via console targeting.

Found two major incompatibility classes: 1) function_call arguments expected as stringified JSON by some SDKs, 2) streaming deltas sometimes merged role+content causing mismatch. Prototype middleware implemented in spike branch spike/cc-hydrator-02.

2026-02-25 @Aisha Rao: Design review notes: prefer deterministic ordering for choices array when multiple model replicas produce responses; add tie-breaker based on latency and model_version weight. Also requested explicit mapping doc for finish_reason values.

Benchmarks show ~0.35ms added median latency for non-streaming path. Streaming path microbenchmark within SLO. Requesting in-review status.

2026-03-09 @Maya Chen: QA pass started. Found edge case where client-supplied 'n' > 1 with streaming true produced interleaved SSE events that some SDKs couldn't reassemble. Added ticket ENG-78235 to address ordering guarantees across multi-choice streaming.
